{"id":"7b2bc98f-a2c0-40a2-9b0f-7dcfcaa21a78","object":"chat.completion","created":1790510244,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"parent_requirement_id": "R2", "mode": "residual", "used_claims": ["C5"], "local_residual": "Whether Ding Lei and his spouse made a foundational gift for the construction of a building that was part of a larger complex."}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need identify one local residual inside Parent Requirement R2. We have claims. Parent: "This person and their spouse, who, up to 2019, had no children from the marriage, made a foundational gift for the construction of a building that was part of a larger complex." Need identify one coherent evidence objective still needed. We need use verified claims. Let's understand.

Original question long chain. R2 focuses on person and spouse made foundational gift for construction of a building part of larger complex, spouse up to 2019 had no children from marriage.

Current claims:
C1 Kwon founded Smilegate, games.
C2 Kwon degree Sogang.
C3 As of June 2025, Kwon listed separated and having 2 children. This conflicts spouse no children up to 2019? It says separated and 2 children as of 2025. Not necessarily spouse no children up to 2019? Could have had children after 2019.
C4 Ding Lei founded NetEase, games.
C5 Ding Lei degree UESTC; at time 2019 article, married but without children.

R2 asks person and spouse made foundational gift for construction of a building that was part of larger complex. We need determine residual. Existing claims support Ding Lei married without children as of 2019. But not that he and spouse made foundational gift for building. Also claim C4 supports Ding founder company whose games division released game etc? Not R2. For Kwon, C3 says separated and 2 children as of 2025; not no children up to 2019. R2 spouse condition: spouse up to 2019 had no children from marriage. C5 establishes for Ding: at time 2019 article married but without children. That covers "spouse, who, up to 2019, had no children from the marriage" maybe. But "made a foundational gift for construction of building that was part of larger complex" is entirely unsupported. So local residual should focus on the foundational gift event: whether [person] and spouse made a foundational gift for construction of a building that was part of a larger complex. Need preserve participants. But we don't know person? Could be Ding Lei likely. But R2 itself says "This person and their spouse..." referent from previous. Since current claims include Ding Lei married no children in 2019. We might select residual: establish that Ding Lei and his spouse made a foundational gift for construction of a building that was part of a larger complex. Should we use used_claims C5? C5 supports spouse no children condition, so use C5. Maybe also C4 supports Ding Lei identity/founder? R2 not about founder. But to tie person? The parent requirement references "This person". The current claims C4/C5 establish Ding Lei as candidate founder? For R2, C5 establishes spouse childless condition for Ding Lei. C4 establishes Ding Lei founder etc. But local residual should be one coherent part. "Ding Lei and his spouse made a foundational gift..." This uses C5? We need used_claims only those that support? We can list C5 because it establishes Ding spouse no children up to 2019, which is part of R2 already established, so not need to re-establish. But residual is gift. used_claims maybe C5 as context for Ding as person/spouse. But if C5 supports one part, yes.

Need decide if mode residual. There is substantive supporting claim. Use C5. Local residual: "Whether Ding Lei and his spouse made a foundational gift for the construction of a building that was part of a larger complex." That's a single coherent evidence objective. But maybe "This person" not yet identified? Original question chain: person who founder of company whose online video games division released game in year... top-earning. Current claims: C4 Ding Lei founded NetEase, games, Fantasy Westward Journey. C5 Ding Lei spouse no children. It seems person likely Ding Lei. But R2 says person and spouse made gift. C5 supports spouse no children. The missing part is gift. We can mention "Ding Lei and his spouse" but if that identification not established by R2? C5 says Ding married without children. C4 says Ding founder etc. Original Q requires founder. So okay.

Could there be multiple independent unresolved parts: the fact that gift was foundational, for construction, building part of larger complex. But that's a single event/relation "made a foundational gift for construction of a building that was part of a larger complex." We can ask to establish that relation. Need not bundle with downstream building university etc.

Should local_residual be a statement? It's an evidence objective, not query. "Establish whether Ding Lei and his spouse made a foundational gift for the construction of a building that was part of a larger complex." That is fine.

Potential issue: Parent Requirement source_span Q2: "This person and their spouse, who, up to 2019, had no children from the marriage, made a foundational gift for the construction of a building that was part of a larger complex." The spouse no children condition maybe already supported for Ding by C5: "at the time of the 2019 article, he was married but without children." That does not explicitly say "spouse had no children from the marriage"; but it implies. Good.

Maybe there is another candidate Kwon. C3 says as of June 2025 separated and 2 children. That doesn't satisfy no children up to 2019. But C1/C2. How to choose? The original question: founder of company whose online video games division released game in specific year, top-earning until 2019, graduated university founded 1930-1970. Kwon: Sogang University founded 1960? Smilegate? Crossfire released 2007, top-earning? Ding: NetEase founded 1997, Fantasy Westward Journey released 2003? top-earning? UESTC founded 1956. Both may fit. R2 spouse no children up to 2019: Ding has C5. Kwon not. So likely person Ding. But R2 doesn't require identifying person? It is about "This person and their spouse..." The evidence context includes both Kwon and Ding. The local residual inside R2 could be "Which person and spouse made a foundational gift..." But since C5 supports Ding's spouse childless, residual likely the gift relation for Ding.

Need JSON:
{
  "parent_requirement_id": "R2",
  "mode": "residual",
  "used_claims": ["C5"],
  "local_residual": "Whether Ding Lei and his spouse made a foundational gift for the construction of a building that was part of a larger complex."
}

Check if used_claims should include C4? C4 says Ding founded NetEase; not R2. But maybe to identify "This person" as Ding. C5 says Ding married without children in 2019. Used claims in schema are claims that support the remaining? They ask "If some part ... already established by Claims, do not ask to establish that part again." used_claims maybe all claims used to identify residual? Example used_claims ["C7"]. We can include C5. Maybe C4 also relevant to person. But R2 only needs spouse condition; C5 establishes spouse childless. C4 does not. The parent requirement refers to person not named; to know that person is Ding maybe from prior requirements. C4/C5 state Ding. C5 alone states Ding and spouse. C4 not needed for R2. But current context includes both. Use C5.

Could local_residual be "The foundational gift by Ding Lei and his spouse for construction of a building within a larger complex" without "whether". That's okay.

Need ensure no search query. Good.
